ταυρογάστωρ.definition: with bull's paunch: metaph., enormous, APl.4.52

ταυροθυτέω.definition: sacrifice a bull or bulls, IG7.2712.22

ταυρόθυτος.definition: at the sacrifice of a bull, Orph.A.614

ταυροκέρκουρος.definition: a kind of river-boat, PCair.Zen.242 , Suid

ταυρόκολλα.definition: glue made from bulls' hides, Plb.6.23.3, Dsc.3.87, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.23.6, Gal.12.832, Paul.Aeg.7.3

ταυροκτόνος.definition: killing bulls, Id.Ph.400; proparox. Pass., killed by a bull, Ammon.Diff.p.129V

ταυρόμορφος.definition: bull-formed, E.Ion1261, cf. Ph.2.160, Ath.11.476a; PMag.Par.1.65

ταυρόομαι.definition: Pass., become savage as a bull, A.Ch.275

ταυροπάρθενος.definition: bull-maiden, i.e. Io, Lyc.1292, cf. Tz. ad loc

ταυροπάτωρ.definition: sprung from a bull, of bees, Theoc.Syrinx3

ταυρόπους.definition: gen. bull-footed, of a rivergod, E.IA275

ταυροπρόσωπος.definition: bull-faced, PMag. Leid.W.1.30, cf. Hermes Trism. in Rev.Phil.32.266; Sch.Par.A.R.2.168

ταυρόπρῳρος.definition: having a bull on the prow, as figurehead, Sch.Lyc.1292

ταυροσφαγέω.definition: cut a bull's throat, cut its throat into a hollow shield, A.Th.43, cf. Sch.Ar.Lys.189

ταυροσφάγος.definition: bull-slaughtering, esp. in sacrifice, S.Tr.609; Lyc.47; of dithyrambic poets, Tz.Diff. Poet.17

ταυροτενής.definition: dub. sens. in Dain Inscr. du Louvre 60.25

ταυροφάγος.definition: bull-eating, epith. of Dionysus, S.Fr.668; applied to Cratinus by Ar.Ra.357

ταυρόφθογγος.definition: bellowing like a bull, sounds that imitate the bellowing of bulls, A.Fr.57.8

ταὐτογραφέω.definition: write in the same way, Eust.45.46

ταὐτοδυναμέω.definition: of words, to be equivalent, mean the same, Sch.E.Or.162

ταὐτοειδής.definition: having the form of identity, Dam.Pr.340. Adv. synonym for ib.349

ταὐτολογέω.definition: repeat what has been said, Plb.1.1.3; Id.1.79.7; Str.12.3.27:—abs., Plb.36.12.2, Phld. Po.Herc.994.30, Hermog.Inv.3.15

ταὐτολογία.definition: = foreg., D.H.Comp.23, Ph.1.529, Quint.Inst. 8.3.50: pl. in Plu.2.504d

ταὐτόνομος.definition: following the same rule, Tz. in An.Par.1.70

ταὐτοπάθεια.definition: reflex signification, Hdn.Gr. ap. An.Ox.3. 271, EM67.44

ταὐτοποδία.definition: repetition of the same foot in the same verse, Sch.Ar.Ra.346, Heph.3.3, Mar.Vict.p.47 K., Atil.Fort. p.280 K

ταὐτοποιέω.definition: act as deputy, PPetr.2p.45; do the same thing, Phld.Po.2.1

ταὐτοπολυλογέω.definition: keep repeating the same thing, Tz.H.10.851

ταὐτοφανής.definition: presenting the appearance of identity, Dam.Pr.241

ταὐτόφωνος.definition: of the same sound, Eust.125.5: hence ib.20

ταφεών.definition: burial-ground, Supp. Epigr.7.161, 167 , OGI642 ; written Supp.Epigr.7.166 :—also IG 12.656

ταφροποιέω.definition: make a trench for besieging, D.S.23.7

ταχύβουλος.definition: hasty in counsel, opp. perh. with allusion to the votes respecting Mytilene , Ar.Ach.630; cf. Max.76

ταχύγηρος.definition: soon becoming decrepit, neut. pl. Hp.Art.58; Gal.6.9; turning grey early, Id.1.328

ταχύγλωσσος.definition: quick of tongue, talking fast, Hp.Epid.2.6.1, Ruf.Fr.70, etc

ταχύγονος.definition: yielding fruit quickly or soon, Thphr.CP4.3.6

ταχυγράφος.definition: shorthand writer, Lyd.Mag.3.6, Stud.Pal. 20.247.2 :—hence write shorthand, Tz.H.8.267, Eust.1607.10

ταχυδρομέω.definition: run fast, Sch.E.Med.1; of Venus, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.133

ταχυθάνατος.definition: liable to sudden death; killing speedily, Hp.Acut.56, Art.66

ταχυκίνητος.definition: moving quickly, Gal.19.631, Porph.in Harm.p.240 W., Adam.2.45

ταχυκρίσιμος.definition: coming quickly to a crisis, Hp.Epid.1.24, Gal.15.172, al

ταχυμάχος.definition: quick to the fray, Hsch. s.v

ταχυπειθής.definition: soon persuaded, credulous; obeying quickly or easily, Tryph.528

ταχύπλοος.definition: contr. fast- sailing, E.Hyps.Fr.1 iii 12, Sch.Od.15.473, Hsch. s.v

ταχύπορος.definition: fast-going, quick of motion, Id.Ag.486, E.El.451; Id.Hel.1272 ; Tim.Pers.175; Hp.Art.11 ; of foods, passing rapidly, Gal.6.535

ταχύποτμος.definition: = Pi.O.1.66; Lyr. Alex.Adesp.34.9, cf. IG14.2005, Nonn.D.48.11

ταχύπωλος.definition: with fleet, swift horses, epithet of the Greeks, Il.4.232, al. ; Theoc.22.136

ταχυφθίμενος.definition: quickly perishing, short- lived, Nonn.D.7.31; ib.11.237

ταχυφυής.definition: healing quickly, of fractures, Hp.Mochl.38, in neut. pl

ταχυχειλής.definition: quick-lipped, flutes or pipes over which the lips run rapidly, AP5.205

ταχύχειρ.definition: gen. quick of hand, nimble, Critias55

ταχυχειρία.definition: quickness of hand, dexterity, Phryn.PSp.111 B., Poll.2.148

τειχοκρατέω.definition: gain possession of a wall, Polyaen.4.2.18

τεκμορεύω.definition: give the sign of loyalty, CR19.420, JHS 32.123, al. , Supp.Epigr.2.750

τεκνοσσόος.definition: driving forth his sons, of agenor, Nonn.D.3.322

τεκνοτροφία.definition: rearing of children, Democr.275, v.l; of animals, rearing of young, Arist.HA562b23

τελεοδρομέω.definition: complete the course, Ps.-Archyt. ap. Iamb.Protr.4

τελεόμηνος.definition: with full complement of months, i.e. a full twelvemonth, S.Tr.824 ; children born after the full number of months, Arist.HA585a20

τελεσσίτοκος.definition: Ep. for completing the birth, Nonn.D.48.890

τελεσσίφρων.definition: perh. perfecting man's mental powers, PMag.Lond.46.415, cf. 121.678

τελεστήριον.definition: place for initiation, at Phlyae; thank-offering for success, X.Cyr.8.7.3, Ael.VH12.1

τελώνιον.definition: custom-house, Posidipp.13, Ev.Matt.9.9; customs-duty, Str.16.1.27, 17.1.16, Harp.s.v

τεμάχιον.definition: Dim. of Hp.Aff.43 , Pl.Smp.191e, Amphis35, Crobyl.8

τεμαχίτης.definition: sliced and salted, Eub.9, Alciphr.3.5, cf. PFlor.388.24

τεμένιος.definition: of or belonging to the; epith. of Hestia, ib.1014.9

τεμένισμα.definition: the precincts of a temple, D.C.42.26, 57.9

τεναγόομαι.definition: Pass., to be formed by shoal-water, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.35

τενθεύω.definition: eat greedily, Poll.6.122, dub. cj. in Lib.Or.62.25

τενοντοκοπέω.definition: cut through the neck, behead, Aq.Ex.34.20: also Id.Ex.13.13

τερατογόνος.definition: favouring the birth of monsters, Vett.Val.18.1

τερατολόγος.definition: marvel-monger, Poll.9.147; Adj., in pass. sense, portentous, Pl.Phdr.229e

τερατόομαι.definition: Med., stare at as a wonder, Timo34

τερατοσκόπος.definition: observer of soothsayer, diviner, Pl.Lg.933c, 933e, Arist.Fr.75, LXXDe.18.11: cf

τερατουργία.definition: working of wonders, Porph.Abst.2.42; use or love of the marvellous, Luc.Icar.6, cf. Plu.2.17b

τερατουργός.definition: wonder-worker, D.S.34/5.2.5, Ptol.Tetr.160, Luc.Gall.4: Adj., Ph.2.267

τερετίζω.definition: twitter, of swallows, Hsch; accompany with the voice, = Phot., Suid

τερετισμός.definition: = foreg., of flutes, trilling, Poll.4.83, cf. Anon.Bellerm.p.26

τριπορνεία.definition: threefold whoredom, by descent, Antiph. Jun. ap. Ath.13.587b

τρισαρειοπαγίτης.definition: an Areopagile thrice over, i. e. a stern and rigid judge, Cic.Att.4.15.4

τρισεινάς.definition: the thrice-ninth day in a month, Hes.Op.814

τρισέληνος.definition: of three moons or nights, epith. of; of three moons in breadth, of the earth's shadow, Plu.2.923b

τρισέπαρχος.definition: thrice an i.e. Praefectus Urbis, AP9.697

τρισκελίς.definition: three-pronged fork, Aq.1 Ki.13.21:—Dim. small tripod, POxy.1066.13

τρισκοπάνιστος.definition: thrice-struck or -stamped, thrice-kneaded, i. e. fine, bread, Batr.35

τρισόλβιος.definition: thrice happy or fortunate, S.Fr.837, Ar.Ec.1129, Philem.93.1, Luc.Nigr.1; divisim, AP12.52

τρισολυμπιονίκης.definition: thrice victorious at Olympia, Pi.O.13.1; Philostr.VA5.8

τρίσοφος.definition: thrice, i. e. very, wise, Tz.H.5.177

τρίσπαστος.definition: drawn threefold, a triple pulley, Orib.49.22.1; so trispastos, Vitr.10.2.3; Tz.H.2.107

τρίσπερμον.definition: with or without name of a plaster, Cass.Fel.34, Paul.Aeg.3.43

τρισσοκέφαλος.definition: three-headed, Orph.A.976 [with the penult. long metri gr.]

τριστάδιος.definition: measuring three stades, Pl.Criti.115e, cf. D.H.1.34

τριστάτης.definition: one who stands next to the king and queen, vizier, LXX4 Ki.7.2, al., cf. Hsch

τρίστεγος.definition: of or with three stories, D.H.3.68; the third story, Act.Ap.20.9:—also Artem.4.46

τριστιχία.definition: triple row, Gal.14.771; union of three verses, Sch.Ar.Ra.326

τρίστοιχος.definition: in three rows, Od.12.91, Ctes; threefold, triple, AP9.668.5 , Orph.A.951; of Cerberus, Hermesian.7.12

τρίστομος.definition: three-edged or three-pointed; dub. sens., prob. place-name, in PTeb.112.2, al. ; Ostr.1097 , cf. BGU1072 iii 2 , etc

τρίστροφος.definition: thrice-twisted, Meges; consisting of three strophes, Sch.Pi.O.9.1

τρισυλλαβία.definition: compass of three syllables, Sch.D.T.p.137 H

τρισύνθετος.definition: compounded of three elements, Sch. D Il.24.540

τρίσχιστος.definition: cloven in three, Sch.Nic.Al.347, An.Ox.2.307:— gloss on Gal.19.71

τρίσχοινος.definition: three long or broad, in neut., Str.17.1.31, cf. Plin.HN5.85

τρισώματος.definition: three-bodied, of Geryon, A.Ag.870; of Cerberus, E.HF24; of the Chimaera, Id.Ion204

τριταγωνιστέω.definition: to be a D.18.262, 265, etc.; play the third part to another, Plu.2.840a

τριταγωνιστής.definition: on the stage, player who took the third part, name of a play by Antiphanes; applied by D. to Aeschines, 18.129, 209

τριταΐζω.definition: have a tertian fever, Dsc.4.60, Gal.7.466

τριταιογενής.definition: produced by tertian fever, Hp.Coac.120. Adv. ib.299

τριταῖος.definition: on the third day, used with Verbs so; three days old, Ar.Fr.387.9; Arist.PA665a35; of three days' standing, Theoc.29.18; after being three days dead, Hdt.2.89

τριταιοφυής.definition: of the nature of a tertian fever, Id.Epid.1.3 ,7, Coac.26

τριταλαντιαῖος.definition: holding three talents, Plu.Aem.33; capable of throwing a weight of three talents, Ph.Bel.51.44

τριτάλαντος.definition: of three talents, Ar.Lys.338; worth three talents, Is.3.18,49

τριτεύς.definition: third part of a IPE12.32A60 , Poll.4.168

τριτεύω.definition: hold the office of CIG3491, IGRom.4.1244 , 414 ; dub. sens. in PStrassb. 114.6

τριτοβάμων.definition: gen. forming a third foot, E.Tr.275 ; cf. II

Τριτογένεια.definition: Trito-born, a name of; the Pythagoreans gave the name to the equilateral triangle, Plu.2.381e; cf

Τριτογενής.definition: collat. form of foreg; prov., apptly. of children born on the third or 23rd of the month , Sch.BT Il.8.39, cf. Suid. s.v

τριτολογέω.definition: in Pass., have one third of one's property confiscated, PGnom. 165

τρίτομος.definition: thrice-cut, IG12.314.108: a kind of tunny, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.139, Plin.HN32.151; = tricodatum, Gloss.; also an object of value, used as a bribe , UPZ62.12

τριτόσπορος.definition: sown for the third time, the third generation, Id.Pers.818

τριτοστάτης.definition: standing third in the chorus, Arist.Metaph.1018b28, Poll.4.106, Simp.in Ph.1268.27:—fem. Ar.Fr.487

τριττυαρχέω.definition: to be head of a III, Pl.R.475a; so IG11.287 B96, 97 , Inscr.Délos 442 B19, 55, al

τριττύαρχος.definition: chief of a III, IG22.641.31 , Poll.8.109; = tribunus, D.H.2.7; of an officer in the army, Lib.Or.25.58

Τριτωνίς.definition: Tritonis, a lake in Libya famous; a spring in Arcadia, also connected by legends with the birth of Athena, Paus.8.26.6

Τριτωνίσκος.definition: small figure of a Triton, on a sun- dial, Inscr.Délos 1417 Ai140

τριφαλαγγία.definition: triple phalanx, i. e. army marching in three phalanxes, Plb.6.40.11, Arr.Tact.28.6, Ael.Tact.36.6, etc

τρίφθογγος.definition: a triple vowel-sound, Tz.H.12.242: as Adj. having three voices, PMag.Par.1.2820

τριφυής.definition: of threefold form, with three stems, of plants, Thphr.HP2.6.9; of the psoas muscle, Gal.2.308: generally, threefold, Orph.H.52.5, Procl.in Prm.p.945S

τρίχαλκον.definition: a coin worth three Thphr.Char.10.6, IG42.109 iii 128 , 5.1433.33 , Vitr.3.1.7

τρίχαλος.definition: Dor. for , cloven in three, = A.Th.760

τρίχαπτος.definition: plaited or woven of; fine veil of hair, IG11.287 A53 , LXXEz.16.10,13, cf. Poll.2.24, 10.32, Hsch

τριχίας.definition: one that is hairy, Poll.4.148 sq; a smaller kind of Arist.HA598b12, Mnesim.4.38 , Dorio ap.Ath.7.328e

τριχιάω.definition: suffer from I, Gal.12.740; suffer from III.1, Arist.HA587b26; of the breasts, Hp.Mul.2.186

τριχίς.definition: a kind of anchovy full of small hair-like bones, Ar.Ach.551, Eq.662; as a mark of a most thrifty person, Eup.154; cf. Arist.HA569b25, and v. II

τριχόβρως.definition: eating hair: hence = or moths, Ar.Ach.1111 )

τριχοειδής.definition: like a hair, Hp.Nat.Hom.14, Arist.HA620b14; of the veins, capillary, Gal.2.808; of nerves, ib.355; Sor.Fract.2; on reptiles, Aët.13.23. Adv. Dsc.4.96

τριχοκόλλημα.definition: a depilatory or eye-salve for the eyelashes, Cass.Fel.29

τριχολάβιον.definition: tweezers for pulling out hairs, Alex.Trall.3.3, Paul.Aeg.6.13, Gloss

τριχολαβίς.definition: = foreg., Orib.Eup.4.20, Gloss.; also Hermes 38.283, Gloss.; dat. Aët.8.53

τριχολογέω.definition: pluck hairs, as the dying do

τριχοποιέω.definition: make, i. e. get, hair, Cass.Pr.50; cause hair to grow, Alex. Trall.1.1, as v.l. for

τρίχορδος.definition: of or with three strings, Anaxil.15 ; Plu.2.1137b

τριχορρυέω.definition: shed the hair, Ar.Pax1222, Andreas ap.Ath.3.115e, Poll.2.26

τριχοτομέω.definition: cut the hair, D.H.7.72; trisect, Papp.56.8, 272.13, Procl.in Euc.p.272 F

τριχοφυέω.definition: grow or get hair, Dsc.1.72, Cleopatra ap.Gal.12.404, Gloss

τριχοφυής.definition: growing or getting hair, Dsc.2.76.18: = Apul. Herb.47

τριχοφυΐα.definition: growth of hair, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.30.6, Gal.12.433

τρίχρονος.definition: in Prosody, of three short syllables, or of one short and one long, Heph.3.1, A.D.Synt.133.27: metaph. of rhythm of pulse, Ruf.Syn. Puls.4.4

τρίχρυσον.definition: gold pentadrachm, worth 60 silver drachmae, PCair.Zen.21.13, 22.6, al

τριχρώματος.definition: three-coloured, Apollod.3.3.1 :—so Luc.DMeretr.9.2, Porph. ap. Eus.PE4.14

τριωβολεῖος.definition: amounting to three obols , POxy.506.12 , BGU362 xv 5

τριώνυχος.definition: with three nails or points, Lyc.392

τριώριον.definition: three hours, Lat. trihorium, Aus.Idyll.10.87, Ep.14.62

τρόχασμα.definition: course, running, App.Anth.6.193 : also Hippiatr.42 , Hsch. s.v

τροχαστής.definition: one who works a water-wheel, PKlein.Form.1197

τροχάω.definition: Ep. form of Arat.1105, APl.4.275 , Anacreont.29.6, etc.; of the stars, revolve, Arat.227

τροχηλασία.definition: locomotion, metaph. of the mutability of human life, Hp.Ep.17

τροχηλατέω.definition: drive a chariot: metaph., drive hither and thither, E.Or.36; Id.El.1253

τροχήλατος.definition: wheel-drawn, A.Pers.1001; dragged by or at the wheels, E.Andr.399

τροχιλεία.definition: block-and-tackle equipment, pulley or system of pulleys, roller of a windlass, and the like , IG12.313.112, 314.123, 374.142, 22.1666.91, 1672.205, al., 11.161 A98 ; the later spelling is found in codd. of Hp.Art.43, …

τρόχις.definition: courier, messenger, acc. A.Pr.941, S.Inach. in PTeb.692 ii 6 , Opp.H.2.634

τρυγήσιμος.definition: ripe for gathering, EM271.32, Hsch. s.v. Gloss

τρυγητής.definition: = I, LXXJe.29.10, al., PTeb.120.8 , Corn.ND30, Poll.1.222

τρύγοιπος.definition: straining-cloth for wine, Ar.Pax535, Pl.1087, Phryn.270, Poll.6.19, 10.75

τρύγω.definition: dry, Theognost.Can.24; but Hsch.; Zonar. Hsch

τρυλίζω.definition: gurgle, of the bowels, Hp.Int.6 ; of the cry of a quail, Poll.5.89

τρυμαλιά.definition: = hole, Sotad.1 , LXXJe.13.4, al.; the eye of the needle, Ev.Marc.10.25; Maria ap.Zos.Alch.p.238 B.; mesh, Aesop.26

τρυπάνιον.definition: Dim. of Archig. ap.Gal.12.821, Phot. s.v

τρυφεραμπέχονος.definition: with soft garments, of the Ionians, Antiph.91

τρυφερεύομαι.definition: Pass., = LXXEs.15.6:—hence in pl., gloss on AB225

τρυφερία.definition: tenderness, etc., Sor.1.10, al.; voluptuousness, Aq.Ge.18.12

τρυφερόβιος.definition: living delicately, luxurious, Phld.Hom.p.23O., cf. AB322, Procl.Par.Ptol.232

τρυφερόσαρκος.definition: with soft, tender flesh or body, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.33

τρυφεροστήμων.definition: gen. of delicate warp or texture, Sch.Lyc.863

τρύχινος.definition: of rags, ragged, J.AJ5.1.16, Gal.Thras.18, Alciphr.1.36

τρυχίον.definition: Dim. of tatter, shred, Hp.Art.47,78, Aret.CA1.2 , 2.2

τρωγλοδύνων.definition: creeping into a hole, of a mouse, interpol. in Batr.52

Τρωΐτης.definition: native of Troia in Egypt, PCair.Zen.133.8

τύκισμα.definition: a working of stones, in pl., i. e. walls of stone worked by rule, E.Tr.814 ; Id.Fr.125.3, cf.HF1096

τύλωμα.definition: glossed by Hsch.; gloss on; sole of the foot, Poll.2.198

τυμβάς.definition: sorceress, witch, so called from their haunting tombs, Hsch

τυμβαύλης.definition: one who plays the flute at a funeral, D.Chr.49.12, Ptol.Tetr.180, Gal.7.241, Ael.VH12.43, etc

τυμβίδιος.definition: at a funeral or tomb, Orph.A.577, H.1.3, 72.5

τύμβιος.definition: in the tomb, CIG1956 ; also BCH48.518

τυμβίτης.definition: on or at the grave, AP7.198

τυμβοφάντης.definition: one who shows a tomb, An.Ox.2.416

τυμπανίας.definition: one who suffers from Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.8.9

τυμπανόομαι.definition: Pass., to be stretched tight like a drum, Hippiatr.71

τυραννησείω.definition: Desiderat. of aspire to sovereignty, Sol. ap. D.L.1.65

τυραννιάω.definition: smack of tyranny; = J.BJ4.7.1, Heraclid.Pol.4, Suid

τυραννίζω.definition: take the part of tyrants, D.17.7

τυραννοδαίμων.definition: tyrant more than human, perh. referring to Aspasia, Com.Adesp.99

τυραννοκτονία.definition: the slaying of a tyrant, Ph. ap. Eus.PE8.14, J.AJ19.1.10, Plu.Pel.34, Luc.Tyr.22

τυρβασία.definition: = II, Poll.4.104, Hsch.; cj. Rzach for in Hes.Fr.96.60

τύρβασμα.definition: trouble, confusion, dub. in Anon.Herc. 418 Fr.2.4

τυροπωλέω.definition: sell like cheese, Ar.Ra.1369: lit., sell cheese, Men.Pk.100

τυροτάριχος.definition: a dish of cheese and salt fish, in Lat. form tyrotarichum, Cic.Att.4.8.1, Fam.9.16.7

Τυροφάγος.definition: Cheese-eater, name of a mouse in Batr.223

τυρόω.definition: make into cheese, curdle, in Pass., Sopat.8; make a mess of , Archestr.Fr.45.13; Hsch

τυφεδών.definition: nonsense, humbug, Neophro Trag; Suid., cf. Theognost.Can.39

τυφλάγκιστρον.definition: blunt hook, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.6.6, 45.18.8, Paul.Aeg.6.5

τυφλίας.definition: a venomous snake, Philum.Ven.29; = Hsch.; cf. sq

τωθασμός.definition: scoffing, jeering, Arist.Pol.1336b17, D.H.3.71, Ph.2.83, Suid

ταυρηδόν.definition: Adv. like a bull, Ar.Ra.804; Pl.Phd.117b

τραπέμπαλιν.definition: Adv. turned backwards, Pherecr.240; to be restored in Plu.2.924c, D.C.47.40

τριάκις.definition: Adv. three times, thrice, Ar.Fr.769, cf. A.D.Adv.146.20; Lacon., acc. to Hsch., and found in IG5.222 : Theognost.Can.160
